answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table per compliance, and regional failover risks dropping in-flight writes during traffic cutover at exactly the moment settlement writes are heaviest	he opposite of the availability-without-write-loss objective. Circuit breakers and read-replica routing address dependency failures or read contention, neither of which matches the observed symptom of a climbing write-path p99 under peak write load. Provisioning additional headroom (memory_b3) is the closest analog: it directly targets write-path saturation without touching the protected release or rerouting live transactions. I want to verify b3's original record to confirm it was specifically about write-path capacity rather than general throughput, and verify b2 to check whether the March failover's clean traffic shift also involved heavy concurrent writes, since that would change the risk calculus. I'm not fully certain added capacity will resolve latency if the security patch itself introduced a write-path regression, so this is a guarded, moderate-scale action rather than a full commitment, and I'm flagging that the root cause may still be release-related and need a follow-up window.
